behavior: Ground-foraging shorebird that walks over wet substrates, rapidly pecking and probing for tiny invertebrates; often migrates and roosts in large flocks, though individuals may aggressively defend feeding space.
field_marks: Very small, plump shorebird with a short neck and small head
Short, straight, dark bill with a blunt-looking tip
Dark eye accented by a weak pale eyebrow
Gray-brown to rusty-brown upperparts with dark mottling or a neat scaly pattern
Pale breast and white belly, with streaking largely confined to the breast
Blackish legs; pointed folded wings reach approximately to the short tail
habitat: Breeds on low tundra near ponds and marshes; during migration and the nonbreeding season, frequents tidal mudflats, estuaries, beaches, sandbars, shallow wetland margins, lakeshores, and wet fields.
